title: Stokes 1999: pcsa of internal oblique at whole (mixed, cadaver)

imaging.modality: Visible Human cryosection images (8-point integration of muscle volumes)
imaging.level_definition: whole muscle split into 6 straight-line components
imaging.posture_detail: cadaver (Visible Human), scaled to standing spine geometry

quantity.name: pcsa
quantity.definition: physiological CSA = muscle volume (mass/density) / fibre length (x cos pennation if stated); PCSA = reconstructed muscle (partial) volume / muscle length (fibres assumed parallel to the component line)

source.sample: 2 Visible Human data sets (1 M, 1 F); abdominal muscle volumes reconstructed from Visible Human male and female cross-sections, geometry scaled to the mean spine of 4 young healthy adults (stereo-radiographs)

how_to_simulate: Sum/compare the PCSA of model abdominal-wall elements (one side) with the component values and totals.
protocol.notes: Table 3 attachment coordinates (X forward, Y left, Z up, origin S1; left side) are not stored here; Table 4 (rib-cage wrapping muscles) is web-only. Transversus abdominis was not represented as straight-line components. Vertebral centre coordinates (Table 1, mean of 4 subjects) not muscle geometry. Volumes (Table 2): EO 171030/220053, IO 93407/138794, TrA 78616/96512, RA 152095/161878 mm3 (F/M).

data.x: total of the six components (Discussion text)

extraction.check_notes: PCSA column re-read from text; units printed "mm" (superscript lost) = mm2.
